items.title: Revise Commvault resource contracts and activation inputs in main.tsp
items.summary: This coarse source-file group changes SaaS activation identifiers and company metadata, CloudAccount creation inputs and PATCH modeling, storage compliance-lock support, and ProtectionGroup/RoleAssignment requiredness. The new preview version and dependency pin describe the applicability of these changes; this mixed group is not a standalone API-version publication or a claim that all changes form one business feature.

inferenceResults.rationale: The three read-only ProtectionGroup member optionality transitions already have dedicated downstream candidates, all judged above. @madeRequired describes their version applicability. No distinct additional wire or SDK candidate is established by this hunk beyond those supplied differences.

This hunk introduces the preview version and its LiftrBase dependency selection. Operations is unchanged diff context. Effective compiler deltas are assessed separately; the version declaration by itself does not establish an additional caller-visible incompatibility.

The roleName/entities requiredness transitions have supplied property candidates. The removed/renamed oldEntities and added entities express the version-specific replacement, with minItems(1) supporting the new input constraint. The permitted evidence does not establish a separate additional generated-SDK member change or mapped AutoRest operation candidate beyond the supplied contract changes, so do not duplicate them.

The removed backupAdminOnCcaCreate and multiPersonAuthorizationOnCcaCreate members already have supplied candidates. company and roleAssignmentsOnCcaCreate are optional additions; their addition alone does not break existing input construction. Requiredness inside the reachable RoleAssignment model is judged separately.

@@typeChangedFrom preserves the old-version projection of the update parameter while the target version uses the changed type. The update parameter and removed request-model identities already have supplied candidates. The augment statement is supporting version metadata, not an additional standalone breaking change.

items.title: Enable visibility-based model splitting for TypeScript generation
items.summary: Enable experimental-split-models-by-visibility for the TypeScript emitter. This is a supporting SDK-generation configuration change, not a REST feature or a new API-version publication.

inferenceResults.rationale: The visibility-splitting option is TypeScript-emitter-specific. Neutral TCGC/AutoRest evidence does not establish the resulting generated TypeScript model names, exports, or import paths. No language-specific break or equivalence can be claimed from this bounded evidence.

findings.actual: Azure.ResourceManager.Foundations.ResourceUpdateModel changed public access, usage, or reachability.
findings.expected: Azure.ResourceManager.Foundations.ResourceUpdateModel preserves its existing language-neutral generated SDK contract.
findings.rationale: The public, reachable CloudAccountUpdate request model disappears when update switches to CloudAccount. Existing callers referring to that request type cannot keep using it. This is not a proven equivalent response-wrapper rename: the request parameter changes nominal type and the supplied old envelope includes tags whereas the target CloudAccount member inventory does not.

guidance.excerpt: The ArmResourcePatch* templates are not recommended. They rely on Lifecycle.Update visibility analysis to automatically determine which properties are included in the PATCH schema, but this analysis is only performed by the typespec-autorest emitter and will not be replicated in SDKs generated for the PATCH operation. Instead, spec authors should define a specific PATCH model and use the ArmCustomPatch* templates.

intentAssessments.title: Retain an explicit request model for CloudAccount PATCH
intentAssessments.expected: The fetched ARM guidance recommends a specific PATCH request model with ArmCustomPatch* rather than ArmResourcePatch*, because implicit Lifecycle.Update filtering in AutoRest is not reproduced by SDK generation. Version decorators separately describe when contract changes apply.
intentAssessments.actual: CloudAccounts.update replaces the custom PATCH request-model template with ArmResourcePatchAsync<CloudAccount>; the supplied neutral SDK facts consequently use CloudAccount rather than CloudAccountUpdate. The same coarse group adds the preview version and version-scoped model/property changes.
intentAssessments.rationale: The changed PATCH template is a concrete mismatch with the fetched SDK-safe modeling recommendation, not a claim that every preview contract change is forbidden. Requiredness decorators and version publication metadata do not remedy the implicit request-model filtering problem. Keep the finding at this intent scope rather than manufacturing findings for each mapped operation.
intentAssessments.gap: The changed PATCH template is a concrete mismatch with the fetched SDK-safe modeling recommendation, not a claim that every preview contract change is forbidden. Requiredness decorators and version publication metadata do not remedy the implicit request-model filtering problem. Keep the finding at this intent scope rather than manufacturing findings for each mapped operation.
